strengths: The virtual-correspondence approach is an original, useful way to construct approximate four-point, three-view solvers from established five-/six-point and P3P solvers. The mean-based variant is especially simple and requires no training. This practical contribution provides the main basis for weak acceptance. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-8wueajbz/call-56f7763ab326403a8f3376f66f89c8d2/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The geometric motivation has meaningful support. The degrees-of-freedom discussion distinguishes calibrated and shared-focal configurations, and supplementary Lemma 1 establishes why the relevant epipolar line intersects the corresponding triangle. The centroid experiments include 10,000 synthetic scenes and 452,500 real-data triangle samples.

The experiments demonstrate practical benefits within GC-RANSAC. On Sacre Coeur, 4p3v(M±0.15) improves median pose error from the HC baseline's 3.04° to 2.42° and AUC@10° from 50.61 to 52.27. On KITTI, it achieves comparable accuracy to 6pt+P3P with lower reported total runtime, 0.07 versus 0.11 seconds. The outlier experiments also support improved convergence per iteration at low inlier ratios.

The evaluation includes substantial comparisons: 10,000 PhotoTourism triplets, noise experiments, perturbation ablations, oracle references, and both solver and pipeline timings. The manuscript explicitly acknowledges approximation error and the circumstances where 5pt+P3P remains preferable. This makes the contribution useful without requiring universal benchmark superiority.
weaknesses: The claim of an advantage under limited computational time is not fully established by the outlier experiments. Figures 3 and 10 compare RANSAC iterations, while hypothesis costs differ substantially: Table 1 reports 218.71 µs for M±0.15 versus 77.90 µs for 5pt+P3P. Error-versus-elapsed-time curves are needed to establish the claimed advantage in this specific regime; aggregate runtimes on other experiments do not settle it.

The shared-focal extension is incompletely validated. Its real-data evaluation uses KITTI stereo/adjacent-frame triplets and reports pose angles without focal-length errors. Parallel or nearly parallel camera configurations can poorly constrain focal length. Additionally, the angular pose metric does not measure the relative translation scale between the two baselines, leaving full three-view reconstruction accuracy untested.

The approximation's operating range remains insufficiently characterized. Figure 6 shows appreciable pose errors even without image noise. The triangle-size bound does not establish small pose error, particularly for poorly conditioned geometry. Aggregate centroid experiments and the evaluated scenes do not isolate sensitivity to depth variation, viewing angle, baseline, or triangle shape.

The learned extension has both a technical ambiguity and a modest demonstrated payoff. Equation (2) defines a signed residual without an absolute value or square; minimizing it as written does not minimize distance to the epipolar line. Whether this is a notation error or the implemented loss is unspecified. Meanwhile, on Sacre Coeur, L±0.1 improves AUC@5° only from the mean-based variant's 44.51 to 44.89 while increasing solver time from 218.71 to 511.28 µs.

Reproducibility is stronger for the basic solver than for the complete experiments. The manuscript supplies network architecture and training settings, but omits important GC-RANSAC thresholds, stopping settings, and local-optimization details. Perturbation values are selected using the reported evaluation scenes, and repeated-run variability is not provided. These omissions complicate assessment of the smaller differences; the promised code release cannot substitute for the supplied evidence.
